chunks: About purchasing fodder crops: a man buys them, then does not cut them, and it occurs to him to leave them until their spikes emerge as barley or wheat. He had bought them from their roots, and whatever land tax was upon their owners was upon the cultivator.

He said: "If, when he bought it, he stipulated that if he wished he could cut it as fodder, and if he wished he could leave it as it is until it becomes spikes, then that is acceptable. Otherwise, it is not proper for him to leave it until it becomes spikes."

key_terms.اشْتَرَطَ: stipulated a condition in the contract
key_terms.الْقَصِيلِ: green fodder crop bought before full maturation
key_terms.حِنْطَةً: wheat as the resulting grain crop
key_terms.خَرَاجٍ: land tax or fiscal due associated with the land
key_terms.سُنْبُلُهُ: its spike or ear, indicating maturation into grain
key_terms.شَعِيرًا: barley as the resulting grain crop

ai.seo_question: Can someone buy fodder crops and later leave them to grow into wheat or barley?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on purchasing green fodder crops and later leaving them to mature into grain. The permissibility depends on whether that option was explicitly stipulated at the time of sale; without such a condition, it is not proper to leave the crop until it forms spikes.
